packageRules.description: Hold every major version bump for manual review — majors carry breaking changes (e.g. a future AGP 10 / Gradle 10, the next Compose BOM major, or another OkHttp/Retrofit major). Surface under Pending Approval and create deliberately; minors/patches keep flowing on schedule.

Keep Kotlin, KSP and Dagger/Hilt coordinated. The AGP 9 / Gradle 9 / Kotlin 2.3 / KSP2 wall was crossed in 2026-07 (see CLAUDE.md 'Toolchain upgrade'), but these stay coupled: KSP is version-locked to the Kotlin compiler, AGP 9's built-in Kotlin resolves KGP from these plugin versions, and Hilt's metadata parser must match the Kotlin metadata version — so a Kotlin bump drags KSP and Hilt with it. This axis has repeatedly broken the build, so group them and hold behind dashboard approval: do the next Kotlin/KSP/Hilt bump deliberately as one PR (also mind Room, which is coupled to kotlinx-serialization, and error_prone_annotations, which Dagger's codegen needs on the compile classpath).

Dagger/Hilt compiler+runtime join the coordinated Kotlin/KSP/Hilt group above. The androidx.hilt:* wrappers are independent and update with AndroidX. NB: the matchDepNames rule above also catches the Hilt Gradle plugin marker `com.google.dagger.hilt.android` — the `com.google.dagger:**` glob here only matches the colon-form artifact coordinates, not the plugin id, which is how the v2.59.2 plugin PR (#14) once slipped past the gate.
All other AndroidX libraries in one PR (includes the androidx.hilt:* wrappers, which are independent of the Dagger/Hilt compiler).
Jetpack Compose (BOM + artifacts) grouped separately from the rest of AndroidX.
security-crypto is alpha; never auto-open a PR — surface it on the dashboard for manual approval. Own groupName so the approval gate doesn't propagate to the rest of the AndroidX group.
